section: Electoral reforms - state funding, electoral bonds, criminalisation of politics, RPA 1951 provisions

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first reported use of an Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) in India?
accepted.x: EVMs were first used on a pilot basis at Parur (Paravur) in Kerala in 1982.
accepted.tq: Use the place-year pair to distinguish the pilot from nationwide implementation.

accepted.s: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, brought about which of the following changes?
o: Reduction of the voting age from 21 years to 18 years
Introduction of Electors' Photo Identity Cards
Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar
accepted.x: The 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years; the change came into force in 1989.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional amendment with its distinctive electoral reform.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC):
1. EPIC was introduced in 1993.
2. Its number, once issued, remains valid for life even if the elector’s address changes.
3. EPIC was introduced through the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EPIC was introduced in 1993, and its number remains valid for life despite a change of address. It was not introduced by the 61st Amendment.
accepted.tq: Separate the year and legal basis of EPIC from the voting-age amendment.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following electoral developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of EPIC
B. EVMs used in all constituencies
C. Introduction of VVPAT and NOTA
D. Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 61st Amendment and voting-age reduction in 1988, EPIC in 1993, nationwide EVM use in 2004, and VVPAT/NOTA in 2013.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest constitutional reform first, then place the technology milestones by year.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for linking electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment.
2. It introduced multiple qualifying dates for registration as an elector.
3. It provided for gender-neutral wording in electoral law.
4. It provided for requisition of premises for election-related purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe provisions associated with the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021.
accepted.tq: Identify the comprehensive option when all listed features belong to the same amendment.

accepted.s: The remote EVM prototype for domestic migrants was shown to political parties during which period?
accepted.x: A remote EVM prototype intended for domestic migrants was demonstrated to political parties in 2022–23.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prototype period from the dates of earlier EVM and VVPAT milestones.

accepted.s: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel consists of:
o: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Union Home Minister
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition
accepted.x: The 2023 Act provides for a panel comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Justice of India was dropped from the panel.
accepted.tq: Use the composition trap by identifying the authority omitted from the final arrangement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2013 — Lily Thomas judgment striking down Section 8(4) of the RPA
2002 — Disclosure of criminal record, assets and education
accepted.x: Electoral bonds were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024; they were not introduced in that year. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed action-year pair, particularly where a later year records invalidation rather than introduction.

accepted.s: The expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in bigger States was raised to which amount in 2022?
accepted.x: In 2022, the expenditure ceiling for a Lok Sabha candidate in bigger States was raised to ₹95 lakh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised ceiling from the corresponding Assembly limit and earlier figures.

accepted.s: ECINET, described as a single platform integrating more than 40 applications, and 100 per cent webcasting are associated with which year?
accepted.x: ECINET, 100 per cent webcasting and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls are identified with 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the digital-election initiative with its year rather than with the year of the CEC selection law.

accepted.s: Under Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate may contest from a maximum of:
accepted.x: Since the 1996 amendment, Section 33(7) permits a candidate to contest from at most two constituencies.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory numerical cap and avoid the pre-1996 position.
accepted.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A candidate elected from both constituencies under Section 33(7) must vacate one of them within:
accepted.x: Under Section 70 of the Representation of the People Act, the candidate must vacate one seat within 14 days after being elected from both constituencies.
accepted.tq: Separate the two-constituency entitlement under Section 33(7) from the time limit under Section 70.
accepted.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following has been proposed as a reform concerning candidates contesting from more than one constituency?
1. One candidate, one seat
2. Requiring the vacating candidate to bear the cost of the resulting by-election
3. Allowing an unlimited number of constituencies if the candidate deposits additional security
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Law Commission proposed the principle of one candidate, one seat, while the Election Commission proposed that a candidate vacating a seat should bear the cost of the by-election. Unlimited contesting was not proposed.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme ‘unlimited’ proposal and retain the two stated reform alternatives.
accepted.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a major provision of the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996?
o: Removal of the limit on constituencies from which a candidate may contest
Reduction of security deposits and proposers for independent candidates
Abolition of by-elections within six months
Capping a candidate’s contest to two constituencies and increasing security deposits
accepted.x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits, and required more proposers for independents and unrecognised parties.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the principal nomination-related changes without reversing them.
accepted.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the amended election law, the poll is countermanded on the death of:
o: A candidate of a recognised political party
A candidate of an unrecognised political party only
accepted.x: The poll is countermanded only when a candidate of a recognised political party dies.
accepted.tq: Focus on the qualification ‘recognised party’ rather than treating the rule as applying to every candidate.
accepted.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Section 135B — Liquor ban for 48 hours before polling
Section 135C — Paid holiday on polling day
Section 70 — Disqualification under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
accepted.x: Section 151A concerns holding a by-election within six months. Section 135B provides for a paid holiday, Section 135C concerns the liquor ban, and Section 70 deals with vacating one of two seats.
accepted.tq: Match statutory sections with their functions and eliminate the swapped-section pairs.
accepted.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding election-day provisions:
1. A paid holiday is provided on the day of poll.
2. Sale of liquor is prohibited during the 48 hours preceding the poll.
3. A by-election is required to be held within six months in the circumstances specified by law.
4. Disqualification may arise for offences under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe provisions associated with election regulation and disqualification under the relevant law.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently, including the less prominent disqualification provision.
accepted.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Section 77 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, is criticised in the context of party expenditure because it:
o: Prohibits all expenditure on election campaigns
Places a ceiling only on the expenditure of candidates, not on the election expenditure incurred directly by political parties
Places a ceiling only on political parties, not on candidates
Requires all campaign expenditure to be incurred in cash
accepted.x: The perceived loophole is that Section 77 caps candidate expenditure while not imposing a comparable ceiling on the parties’ own election spending.
accepted.tq: Ask who bears the statutory ceiling to expose the candidate-party distinction.
accepted.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For a political party to retain tax exemption under the stated provisions, which combination is relevant?
o: No donation above ₹2,000 in any form and no record of larger donations
No cash donation above ₹20,000 and records only of donations above ₹2,000
No cash donation above ₹2,000 and proper records of donations above ₹20,000
Acceptance of unlimited cash donations provided they are reported after the election
accepted.x: The stated conditions include no cash donation above ₹2,000 and maintenance of records for donations above ₹20,000. These are referred to under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, replacing the earlier reference to Section 13A of the 1961 Act.
accepted.tq: Keep the two monetary thresholds separate instead of reversing their functions.
accepted.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a method of evading the donation-recording threshold?
o: Restricting all campaign publicity to official election broadcasts
Converting all party donations into government grants
Splitting a large gift into several gifts below ₹20,000 and diverting funds through surrogate digital advertisements or paid news
Depositing every donation directly into the Consolidated Fund of India
accepted.x: Evasion may occur by splitting large gifts into amounts below ₹20,000 and by diverting money through surrogate digital advertisements and paid news.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical loophole that exploits the threshold and indirect campaign channels.
accepted.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the Association for Democratic Reforms’ assessment cited in relation to party funding, what share of party funds during 2004–23 came from undisclosed sources?
accepted.x: The cited ADR assessment states that 60 per cent of party funds, amounting to ₹19,083 crore, came from undisclosed sources during 2004–23.
accepted.tq: Test the paired percentage and absolute amount together to prevent partial recall.
accepted.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court struck down the electoral bonds scheme in February 2024 in which case?
o: Tarkunde Committee v Union of India
Lily Thomas v Union of India
accepted.x: The electoral bonds scheme was struck down by the Supreme Court in Association for Democratic Reforms v Union of India in February 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the case concerning electoral bonds from the cases concerning NOTA and disqualification.
accepted.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In PUCL v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court directed that voters should have the option of:
o: Voting twice, once for a candidate and once for a party
Choosing the Chief Election Commissioner directly
Rejecting all candidates through a ‘None of the Above’ option on ballots and EVMs
Requiring a fresh election whenever NOTA receives the highest votes
accepted.x: PUCL v Union of India led to the provision of a ‘None of the Above’ option on ballot papers and EVMs. It did not mandate re-election when NOTA is highest.
accepted.tq: Separate the right to express rejection from the unrelated consequence of automatically holding a fresh poll.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court located the right to reject candidates through NOTA primarily in which constitutional provision?
accepted.x: The right to reject was linked to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).
accepted.tq: Match the electoral expression right with the constitutional freedom that supports it.

accepted.s: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections in which set of States and Union Territory?
o: Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi
Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi
Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Haryana, Maharashtra and Delhi
Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Puducherry
accepted.x: The first use of NOTA was in the 2013 Assembly elections in Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.
accepted.tq: Use the complete geographical set to distinguish the first Assembly use from later nationwide use.

accepted.s: NOTA was used for the first time in a Lok Sabha election in:
accepted.x: NOTA was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014, after its initial use in the 2013 Assembly elections.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first Assembly-election year from the first Lok Sabha-election year.
